newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed in dull trading on Thursday with most investors taking a wait-and-see attitude, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 21,470 yuan ($2,587) per tonne, losing 10 yuan. It opened at 21,450 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 21,400 and a high of 21,560.
January rose 10 to 20,800, February fell 20 to 20,920, March was down 60 at 21,190, May increased 10 to 21,570 and June 10 to 21,600.
Combined volume fell sharply to 25,560 from 105,050.
Copper opened mixed and moved around the opening levels for most of the session.
Traders said investors were waiting for further market-moving news, with few daring to build large long positions.
"Thin volume indicated many investors are sticking to the sidelines," a trader said.
Traders said some long liquidation emerged on the market given the the lack of further rises on the London Metal Exchange last night after gains in the previous session.
"There was no further positive market-moving news after the sharp gains on Wednesday, resulting in some profit-taking on disappointment," a second trader said.
"Many investors doubt if copper will maintain an upward trend in the short term with the approach of the Chinese lunar new year holiday," he added.
Traders expect Shanghai copper to follow the LME's trend in the next few days due to the absence of domestic market-moving news.
Aluminium ended sharply up. January rose 380 to 14,530 yuan per tonne, February 410 to 14,810, March 260 to 15,210 and April 410 to 15,650.
Combined volume rose to 3,040 tonnes from 800.
